blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how your phone can store energy to power your apps and games? Capacitors are key to this process!

blocks.markdown: Capacitors are devices used to store electrical energy in an electric field. They are widely used in electronic circuits for various applications, such as filtering and energy storage.

blocks.title: Definition of Capacitance
blocks.text: Capacitance is the ability of a capacitor to store charge per unit voltage. It is measured in farads (F), where 1 farad equals 1 coulomb per volt.

blocks.markdown: The relationship between charge, capacitance, and voltage in a capacitor is given by the formula $Q = CV$, where $Q$ is the charge in coulombs, $C$ is the capacitance in farads, and $V$ is the voltage in volts.

blocks.title: Calculating Charge Stored in a Capacitor
blocks.prompt: A capacitor with a capacitance of 5 microfarads is connected to a 12-volt battery. Calculate the charge stored in the capacitor.

steps.text: Identify the given values: $C = 5 \times 10^{-6}$ F, $V = 12$ V.
Use the formula $Q = CV$ to calculate the charge.
Calculate the result: $Q = 60 \times 10^{-6}$ C or $60$ microcoulombs.

blocks.answer: The charge stored in the capacitor is 60 microcoulombs.

blocks.markdown: Capacitors can be combined in series or parallel to achieve desired capacitance values. The effective capacitance of capacitors in series is less than any individual capacitor, while in parallel, it is the sum of all capacitances.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember that for capacitors in series, the reciprocal of the total capacitance is the sum of the reciprocals of individual capacitances. For parallel, simply add the capacitances.

points: Capacitance is the ability to store charge per unit voltage, measured in farads.
The formula $Q = CV$ relates charge, capacitance, and voltage.
In series, the effective capacitance is less than any single capacitor; in parallel, it is the sum of all capacitances.
